new.title: Walk Perret's UNESCO rebuilt centre of Le Havre
new.desc: The city centre was rebuilt from 1945 by Auguste Perret and inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2005, covering about 133 hectares. Its centrepiece is the Hôtel de Ville, built 1952-1958 and completed by Jacques Tournant after Perret's death, with a 72-metre belfry.
new.tip: Start at the Hôtel de Ville and follow Avenue Foch; the Maison du Patrimoine on place Perret has maps and guided tours.
new.q: Hôtel de Ville, Place de l'Hôtel de Ville, Le Havre

new.title: Look up inside Perret's Église Saint-Joseph, Le Havre
new.desc: Perret's concrete church has an octagonal lantern tower about 107 metres high, one of the tallest church towers in France. Built from 1951 and finished after his death in 1954, it is lit by roughly 12,000 coloured glass panes.
new.tip: Visit on a sunny day for the best light under the tower; the church sits on boulevard François Ier.
new.q: Église Saint-Joseph, Boulevard François 1er, Le Havre

new.title: See Impressionists at the MuMa in Le Havre
new.desc: The Musée d'art moderne André Malraux opened in 1961 in a glass-and-steel building by Guy Lagneau at the harbour entrance. It holds one of the richest Impressionist collections in France outside Paris, with Monet, Boudin and Dufy.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; check muma-lehavre.fr for hours. Allow two hours.
new.q: MuMa, 2 Boulevard Clemenceau, Le Havre

new.title: Stroll the Jardins Suspendus in Le Havre's old fort
new.desc: The gardens occupy the Second Empire Fort de Sainte-Adresse, abandoned by the army in 1972 and bought by the city in 2000. Opened as gardens in 2008, they carry the Jardin Remarquable label and overlook the port, the Seine estuary and the sea.
new.tip: Main entrance is on rue du Fort; there is a tea room, and bus lines 4 and 5 stop nearby.
new.q: Les Jardins Suspendus, Rue du Fort, Le Havre

new.title: Climb to the Porte d'Aval and Aiguille, Étretat
new.desc: The Falaise d'Aval ends in the Porte d'Aval arch, with the chalk needle of the Aiguille Creuse standing just offshore. The Aiguille inspired Maurice Leblanc's 1909 Arsène Lupin novel L'Aiguille creuse.
new.tip: Stairs from the west end of the beach lead to the top; stay on the path, as walking under the cliffs is banned.
new.q: Falaise d'Aval, Étretat

new.title: Visit Notre-Dame de la Garde chapel on Étretat's Falaise d'Amont
new.desc: The chapel on the Falaise d'Amont was built in the 1850s for sailors, destroyed in the Second World War and rebuilt in the 1950s. Next to it stands the white arrow monument to Nungesser and Coli, whose plane L'Oiseau Blanc was last seen here in 1927.
new.tip: The museum of Étretat's heritage on the same cliff is open at weekends; come at sunset for the view over the Porte d'Aval.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame de la Garde, Falaise d'Amont, Étretat

new.title: Wander the Jardins d'Étretat above the cliffs
new.desc: Opened to the public in September 2016, the gardens are set on the Amont cliff and divided into seven themed sections with sculptures and sea views. The site carries the Jardin Remarquable label.
new.tip: Open seasonally (the 2026 season runs from July to early November); check etretatgarden.fr before going.
new.q: Les Jardins d'Étretat, Avenue Damilaville, Étretat

new.title: Tour the Palais Bénédictine and taste the liqueur, Fécamp
new.desc: The Palais Bénédictine combines a museum, a working distillery and cellars where the herbal liqueur is made. The tour ends with a tasting, and a contemporary art exhibition is part of the visit.
new.tip: Booking is advised; the Discovery tour takes about two hours. Address: 110 rue Alexandre Le Grand.
new.q: Palais Bénédictine, 110 Rue Alexandre Le Grand, Fécamp

new.title: Step inside Fécamp's Abbatiale de la Sainte-Trinité
new.desc: The abbey church is a major pilgrimage site tied to the Precious Blood relic, which legend says arrived in a fig-tree trunk. The reliquary was stolen in 2022 and returned on 13 September 2023.
new.tip: The reliquary is shown only for the feast of the Precious Blood in mid-June.
new.q: Abbatiale de la Sainte-Trinité, Rue Alexandre Le Grand, Fécamp

new.title: Discover Lutyens and Jekyll at the Bois des Moutiers, Varengeville
new.desc: Guillaume Mallet created the estate from 1898 with architect Edwin Lutyens, who designed the house and pergola, and garden designer Gertrude Jekyll. It is a rare example of English Arts and Crafts gardening in France, with about 12 hectares.
new.tip: Opening is seasonal; check boisdesmoutiers.com for current access before you go.
new.q: Le Bois des Moutiers, Route de l'Église, Varengeville-sur-Mer

new.title: Admire the Renaissance Manoir d'Ango in Varengeville
new.desc: This Renaissance manor was built for the Dieppe shipowner Jean Ango in the 16th century and is a listed historic monument. It is known for its courtyard and dovecote.
new.tip: Tickets were about 6 euros for a self-guided visit; confirm hours with the Dieppe tourist office.
new.q: Manoir d'Ango, Varengeville-sur-Mer

new.title: Browse Dieppe's ivory carvings in the Château-Musée
new.desc: The castle above the seafront houses a museum known for its collection of Dieppe ivories, carved from the 16th to the 20th centuries, among the largest in Europe. Ship models, fans and devotional statuettes are on display.
new.tip: Check hours on the Dieppe tourism site before going.
new.q: Château-Musée de Dieppe, Rue de Chastes, Dieppe

new.title: Marvel at Dieppe's Gothic Église Saint-Jacques
new.desc: Work on this church began around 1191, with additions from the 13th to the 16th century. The flamboyant west front with a rose window and tall belfry is the highlight; it has been a monument historique since 1840.
new.tip: Entry is free outside services; combine it with the Grande Rue market on Saturdays.
new.q: Église Saint-Jacques, Place Saint-Jacques, Dieppe

new.title: Tour the Château d'Eu and its Louis-Philippe museum
new.desc: The city of Eu bought the château in 1964 and the Louis-Philippe museum opened in 1973 in the main wing. It recalls Queen Victoria's 1843 visit, a milestone in Franco-British friendship.
new.tip: Closed Tuesdays; the ground floor is accessible. Official site chateau-eu.fr.
new.q: Château d'Eu, Place Isabelle d'Orléans-Bragance, Eu

new.title: Descend into the crypt of Eu's Collégiale Notre-Dame et Saint-Laurent
new.desc: The Gothic collegiate church holds a 12th-century crypt with the tomb of Saint Laurent O'Toole, archbishop of Dublin, who died at Eu in 1180. The effigies of the counts of Eu are also in the crypt.
new.tip: Crypt visits depend on religious services; ask at the church or the tourist office.
new.q: Collégiale Notre-Dame et Saint-Laurent, Rue Saint-Laurent, Eu

new.title: Ride the free funicular up to Le Tréport's cliff belvédère
new.desc: The funicular rises about 100 metres up the chalk cliff in two minutes and is free. The viewpoint at the top gives a view over roofs, harbour and Mers-les-Bains, and the Calvaire des Terrasses crowns the cliff.
new.tip: It runs from about 7:45; the climb on foot is 378 steps.
new.q: Funiculaire du Tréport, Quai François Ier, Le Tréport

new.title: Eat raie crème et câpres at Le Bistrot des Halles, Le Havre
new.desc: Traditional bistro on the square of the Halles Centrales, the covered market built 1958-1960 in the Perret reconstruction. Specialities cited include côte de boeuf, bone marrow, skate in cream and caper sauce and squid à l'armoricaine.
new.tip: Go after a market morning; the Halles close at 13:00 on Sundays.
new.q: Le Bistrot des Halles, 7 Place des Halles Centrales, Le Havre

new.title: Order a seafood platter at La BDH, Le Havre
new.desc: La BDH (Brasserie des Halles) is a Maître Restaurateur brasserie on the Halles Centrales square, known for seafood and traditional cooking. It is one of few Le Havre restaurants recognised by the Collège Culinaire de France.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; a first menu was listed at 21.90 euros.
new.q: La BDH, 25 Place des Halles Centrales, Le Havre

new.title: Try vivier lobster at Le Homard Bleu, Étretat
new.desc: Seafront restaurant facing the Falaise d'Aval, serving lobster from its tank and homemade seafood dishes.
new.tip: Book ahead on summer weekends and ask for a table with a cliff view.
new.q: Le Homard Bleu, Front de Mer, Étretat

new.title: Slurp oysters at L'Huitrière, Étretat
new.desc: Sea-view restaurant opened in 2010 on rue Traz Périer, known for oysters and seafood platters, with large windows toward the cliffs.
new.tip: Weekend lunch and dinner service was listed; reserve for sunset.
new.q: L'Huitrière, 11 Rue Traz Périer, Étretat

new.title: Eat moules à la crème at Le Barbican on Fécamp's quay
new.desc: Seafood bistro on Quai Bérigny facing the harbour, listed by Gault&Millau and Seine-Maritime Tourisme.
new.tip: Closed Sundays per local listings; try the Fécamp-style mussels in cream.
new.q: Le Barbican, 97 Quai Bérigny, Fécamp

new.title: Order Dieppe scallops at Le Turbot in the Pollet
new.desc: Fish restaurant on quai de la Cale in the old fishermen's quarter of Pollet, whose reviewers single out the coquilles Saint-Jacques. Gault&Millau rates it 11/20.
new.tip: Budget around 27-32 euros; try the scallops, in season October to May.
new.q: Le Turbot, 14 Quai de la Cale, Dieppe

new.title: Taste saint-pierre and scallops at Bistrot du Pollet, Dieppe
new.desc: Small bistro on rue Tête de Boeuf that Gault&Millau praised for a perfectly executed saint-pierre and scallop dish, rated 4.5/5 on Petitfute.
new.tip: Book ahead; the Pollet quarter is a short walk across the bridge from the harbour.
new.q: Bistrot du Pollet, Rue Tête de Boeuf, Dieppe

new.title: Spoon up the marmite du Quai at Quai 11, Dieppe
new.desc: Brasserie opened in 2022 facing the marina, serving a marmite of langoustine, salmon and fish of the day in sauce dieppoise.
new.tip: Open for lunch most days; waiting times can be long at busy services.
new.q: Quai 11, 11 Quai Henri IV, Dieppe

new.title: Have moules-frites at La Marine on Le Tréport's quay
new.desc: Popular quayside restaurant serving traditional seafood, fish and meat menus at competitive prices; the mussels are the most-ordered dish.
new.tip: Quai François Ier is the harbour front lined with fish restaurants; check hours before going.
new.q: La Marine, 52 Quai François 1er, Le Tréport

new.title: Eat sole meunière at Le Homard Bleu, Le Tréport
new.desc: Quai François Ier seafood restaurant known for blue lobster, seafood platters, sole meunière and scallops.
new.tip: Reserve for weekend lunches.
new.q: Le Homard Bleu, 45 Quai François 1er, Le Tréport

new.title: Eat Veules oysters at Le P'tit Veulais
new.desc: Traditional restaurant using local produce, with oysters from Veules-les-Roses and fish and scallops from the local coast.
new.tip: Veules oysters are grown in the village; try them with a walk along the river afterwards.
new.q: Le P'tit Veulais, 1 Rue du Docteur Girard, Veules-les-Roses

new.title: Try buckwheat galettes at Crêperie La Gouanière, Saint-Valery-en-Caux
new.desc: Crêperie on rue Jacques Angot making galettes from buckwheat flour cooked on site, with praise for homemade crêpes.
new.tip: Hours are seasonal; check before you go.
new.q: Crêperie La Gouanière, 5 Rue Jacques Angot, Saint-Valery-en-Caux

new.title: Eat fish facing the port at Les Flots, Saint-Valery-en-Caux
new.desc: Restaurant on Quai d'Amont facing the fishing port, offering traditional Norman cuisine with a fish and seafood speciality.
new.tip: Set menus run from about 30 to 40 euros.
new.q: Les Flots, 18 Quai d'Amont, Saint-Valery-en-Caux

new.title: Swim and stroll the pebble beach of Le Havre
new.desc: The Plage du Havre stretches about two kilometres of pebbles and sand from the port towards Sainte-Adresse. Supervised bathing in season, Blue Flag since 2003.
new.tip: Open 6:00-19:00; check the flag before swimming. The Promenade Maritime runs along it.
new.q: Plage du Havre, Boulevard Clemenceau, Le Havre

new.title: Paddle on Monet's Sainte-Adresse beach
new.desc: A large pebble beach at the north-west tip of Le Havre, supervised for bathing in season and painted by Monet in 1867. Buses from central Le Havre serve it.
new.tip: Parking is hard in summer; take the LiA bus. Nudism is banned.
new.q: Plage de Sainte-Adresse, Boulevard Albert 1er, Sainte-Adresse

new.title: Walk the Aval and Amont cliff loop above Étretat
new.desc: A loop over both cliffs passes the Porte d'Aval and the Amont chapel, with views of the Aiguille. Visorando lists a loop of about 12 km, and the GR21 runs along this coast.
new.tip: Stay on the path and away from the edges; landslides are a risk.
new.q: Plage d'Étretat, Boulevard René Coty, Étretat

new.title: Take the GR21 cliff path from Yport towards Étretat
new.desc: Yport is a small fishing village between Fécamp and Étretat with a pebble beach, painted boats and fresh-water springs at low tide. The GR21 climbs from the village to the cliff-top path to Étretat.
new.tip: Regional bus 509 links Le Havre and Fécamp; on 15 August the village holds its Fête de la Mer.
new.q: Plage d'Yport, Yport

new.title: Browse Dieppe's Saturday market on the Grande Rue
new.desc: The Saturday market fills the pedestrian Grande Rue, rue Saint-Jacques and place Nationale from about 8:30 to 13:00 with fresh and local produce including fish and Neufchâtel cheese. It was named one of the most beautiful markets in France in 2018.
new.tip: Come early on Saturday morning; street traders return in the afternoon.
new.q: Grande Rue, Dieppe

new.title: Follow France's shortest river in Veules-les-Roses
new.desc: The Veules runs about 1,149 metres from its watercress springs to the sea past mills and flowered cottages. The village was voted most beautiful village of France in 2017.
new.tip: Walk the Chemin des Cressonnières from the source to the beach.
new.q: Chemin des Cressonnières, Veules-les-Roses

new.title: Join Fécamp's Herring and Scallop Festival
new.desc: Each November the quays host grilled herring, scallops, traditional smoking demonstrations in the Boucane tradition and direct sales by fishermen, drawing more than 40,000 visitors. The 2026 edition is 28-29 November.
new.tip: Free entry; eat at the quay stalls and visit the Musée des Pêcheries.
new.q: Quai Sadi Carnot, Fécamp

new.title: Taste Neufchâtel AOP at the Fête du Fromage
new.desc: The annual Neufchâtel-en-Bray cheese festival (31st edition on 19-20 September 2026) offers tastings of Neufchâtel AOP, the heart-shaped Pays de Bray cheese.
new.tip: Held in the town centre; check the programme with the tourist office.
new.q: Place Notre-Dame, Neufchâtel-en-Bray

new.title: Hike to the Phare d'Ailly from Sainte-Marguerite-sur-Mer
new.desc: A 4.7 km loop from Sainte-Marguerite beach crosses the Bois d'Ailly nature reserve to the cape and its 19.5 metre lighthouse above 30 metre chalk cliffs. Longer routes continue on the GR21 to Varengeville.
new.tip: The Vastérival variant at the cliff foot is only possible at low tide.
new.q: Plage de Sainte-Marguerite-sur-Mer, Sainte-Marguerite-sur-Mer

new.title: Cycle the Avenue Verte London-Paris from Forges-les-Eaux
new.desc: The flat, paved voie verte of the Pays de Bray follows the disused Dieppe-Paris railway; the Avenue Verte starts here. About 56 km lead to Dieppe, with a ferry to Newhaven from the port.
new.tip: Check the Forges-les-Eaux tourist office for bike hire and route guides.
new.q: Avenue Verte, Forges-les-Eaux

new.title: Ride the Circuit du Neufchâtel through Pays de Bray farms
new.desc: A 75 km cycling circuit links cheese-making sites and farm shops of the Pays de Bray, where Neufchâtel AOP is made.
new.tip: Ask the tourist office in Neufchâtel-en-Bray for the route and farm opening times.
new.q: Office de Tourisme, Neufchâtel-en-Bray

new.title: Walk the cliff viewpoints of Saint-Valery-en-Caux
new.desc: A route links the 1962 boat-roofed Chapelle Notre-Dame du Bon Port to chalk cliff viewpoints over the Channel, the port and the town.
new.tip: Start at the chapel on Place de la Chapelle.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame du Bon Port, Place de la Chapelle, Saint-Valery-en-Caux

new.title: Relax at the lake beach of Forges-les-Eaux
new.desc: A landscaped beach around a lake at the Domaine de Forges, in a former spa town known for its iron-rich springs. Boats can be hired, and a casino stands in the domain.
new.tip: Avenue des Sources; boat hire in season.
new.q: Plage de Forges-les-Eaux, Avenue des Sources, Forges-les-Eaux
